referents.why: 'tell him': the one addressed by Moses's saying is Pharaoh (w13).
'my people' is first person in the LORD's words, which Moses delivers; the speaker of those words is the LORD (w25).
referents.category: first person in a quoted divine speech

referents.why: 'that they may serve me' is first person in the same quoted divine speech: the LORD.
referents.category: first person in a quoted divine speech

referents.why: Implied 'you' of 'rise early' is the one the LORD speaks to, Moses (w4).
Second masculine singular weqatal 'you will say': Moses (w4), who is commanded to speak to Pharaoh.
The imperative 'let my people go' is addressed to the one Moses speaks to, Pharaoh (w13).
referents.category: implied you inside quoted divine speech

referents.why: Third masculine plural 'that they may serve me' refers to the people (w27), a collective singular noun that takes plural verbs in Hebrew.

links.why: Reversed and cross-verse: cl0 opens the verse as a wayyiqtol continuing from the previous verse, and across verses the link is the episode rung.
Two imperatives of one person joined by waw: plain and.
cl4 is the participle inside the temporal clause 'when Pharaoh goes out'. The weqatal 'you will say' continues the commands of cl2, not that clause.
links.category: command continuation across a temporal clause

links.why: Second-person weqatal after imperatives, same person: plain and, one level of commands.
The LORD's words to Moses are a collection of commands (rise, present, say): the content is the whole imperative group.
links.category: speech content of a collection of commands

links.why: 'You will say to him' introduces the message, the said clause 'thus says the LORD'.
'Thus says the LORD' introduces the quoted command 'let my people go', the said clause.
A command joined to a change of person is so that, not a plain and.
links.category: command joined to a change of person

links.why: Imperative then waw plus yiqtol in a different person: what the release is for.

groups.why: The LORD speaks to Moses. The commanded speech Moses is to give Pharaoh is nested as a part, and the commands to Moses are a part.
Rise early, present yourself, and you will say: commands joined by and at one level form one group. The builder's part was not a role of that kind.
The innermost turn is the LORD's message, quoted by Moses: its sender is the LORD and its addressee Pharaoh (R2).
Let my people go, so that they may serve me: one command with its aim. The builder's part was not a role of that kind.
Moses is commanded to speak to Pharaoh, so the commanded turn is his, with the LORD's message as its part (R2 and nested speech).

none_fit.where: cl3 and cl4 (hinneh 'there' plus a bare participle, 'when Pharaoh goes out to the water')
none_fit.what: A temporal clause setting the time of the command in cl2. No link type covers a when-clause that is neither a condition nor a nested role, so it is left unlinked.
